enterfront.body: This project is a simple chat application. It uses pseudo-database (API with a local variable) and short-pulling to access messages. Registration is performed also via API with the use of tokenization.
enterfront.history: It was an elective course Enterprise Programming on JS I have chosen at the the Fall semester 2024. I was in a team of 3 people, we were working during the period of 2 months.
enterfront.ps: Project should work properly, try it! Register (or use one of predefined users e.g. 'alice' with password'1234') and type some id to start chatting (e.g. 'alice', 'evead', 'frank').

textyle.body: The idea is relatively simple: insert a text in any style, than convert it to the desired one. Then applying AI model that was connect with backend technics on Rust to the frontend on React.
textyle.history: This project was chosen as a topic of a Practicum Project course that was conducted in Summer 2024. We had 7 people at our team: team-leader, 2 frontend developers, 2 backend developers, 2 AI programmers.
textyle.ps: Unfortunately, the backend server as well as AI model wasn't hosted and ran locally during the presentation. Nevertheless, you can watch a video prepared for the final submission and demonstration.

fwd.body: This project doesn't pursue a complex idea, it's just demonstrating basic skills at the Frontend development. A user can observe a variety of different dishes that are published by restaurant admins. They can add it to their cart and calculate calories and price. Admins can post different dishes.
fwd.history: This is the final project for an elective course related the Frontend I took in Summer 2023. There was a small team of 2 people. However, for me this course and the project in particular were a starting point in the Frontend Development.
fwd.ps: The website works properly till the current but some links for meals are outdated and nonworking that's why some images are not displayed.

booking.body: The idea of the project: provide a convenient way to make bookings of university rooms for students and stuff. It was a telegram bot (with a Web App) that connected to an API related to bookings.
booking.history: It was a summer project (2023) at the core course for a team of 5. There were 2 frontend developers, including me.
booking.ps: There is no support for telegram bot anymore, however there is still a video about it. Enjoy watching it!

sna.short: System for periodical change of passwords
sna.body: This is an encoding systems that can periodically change password keys for security. It is used to create, store, and automatically update keys using a scheduler (a key updates once a day). It was implemented via Telegram Bot on Linux OS.
sna.history: I was working on this project during a course named Software Networks and Administration. I was the author of an idea for a project and the implementor of the hardest part of it (working with scheduler on Linux and returning updated code).
sna.ps: Initially, there wasn't even an idea to somehow host it, so there is only a video. It is relatively big (there were requirements of the course) but the most interesting part is at 6:25 (my college have explained before in the video that we have set update time to 22:27 instead of 00:00).

enigma.short: A Model of the Enigma machine
enigma.body: The Machine has 3 active rotors (you need to choose out of 5), that rotates after pressing any key. When the first rotor makes full rotation, it rotates the second rotor on one position and so on. You need to enter letters one-by-one, then you will receive the output.txt with the encoded text. Repeat procedure to decipher.
enigma.history: I had seen a film about encoding and deciphering and wanted to dive deeper in this theme, so I wrote a C++ project that demonstrates how the Enigma machine works.
enigma.ps: I was practicing my German, so the video is only in German.
